projectName: Web Ledger, Transaction Entry, and Wallet Management
description: Bring the operational editing surfaces to the web: ledger browsing, transaction details, manual entry flows, and wallet CRUD/rename/merge so the web app can serve routine management without losing TUI fallback safety.

timing.gatingCondition: Proceed after foundation, tax, and portfolio features establish stable auth, navigation, and JSON model conventions.

principles: Operational Confidence - every write flow must be explicit, validated, and auditable
Wallets Are First-Class - preserve explicit wallet management because 2025+ tax rules depend on it
Safe Destructive Actions - rename, merge, delete, and restore flows require strong confirmation
TUI Logic, Web Presentation - the web layer calls existing Python write/query services rather than duplicating transaction logic
Desktop Depth, Mobile Utility - browsing and quick-entry should work on phone; dense table operations get richer desktop treatment

techStack.frontend: Responsive web UI with table/filter forms and modal/detail flows
techStack.testing: pytest API tests + frontend smoke tests

userStories.title: Ledger explorer API and responsive web table
acceptanceCriteria: Expose ledger endpoint with filters for coin, wallet, date range, and deleted visibility
Return normalized transaction JSON rather than TUI column labels
Support pagination suitable for phone and desktop
Preserve soft-delete visibility and filtering semantics
userStories.testStrategy: pytest ledger endpoint tests with filter combinations and deleted rows

userStories.title: Transaction detail, edit, delete, and restore flows
acceptanceCriteria: Show detail view for one transaction with all accounting fields
Allow edit of supported fields with diff preview or equivalent confirmation
Allow soft-delete and restore through authenticated write endpoints
Warn clearly before actions that can affect transfer-pair integrity or tax interpretation
userStories.testStrategy: pytest transaction write API tests and UI confirmation-flow checks

userStories.title: Manual transaction entry flows
acceptanceCriteria: Provide buy, sell, transfer, and interest-income forms on the web
Reuse wallet dropdown/new-wallet patterns from the TUI behavior
Validate required numeric and wallet fields before write
Show concise success feedback and refresh related portfolio/tax views
userStories.testStrategy: pytest transaction creation API tests + frontend form smoke tests

userStories.title: Wallet management on the web
acceptanceCriteria: Expose wallet CRUD endpoints and web screens for create, edit, activate/deactivate, rename, and merge
Show transaction counts and warnings on rename/merge flows
Call sync_wallets_from_ledger where needed so existing ledgers remain manageable
Preserve wallet metadata needed for tax and custody visibility
userStories.testStrategy: pytest wallet API tests with rename/merge transaction assertions

userStories.title: Audit and safety polish for write operations
acceptanceCriteria: Log or persist operator-visible metadata for destructive actions where appropriate
Ensure failed writes roll back cleanly
Document expected behavior for concurrent writes in PostgreSQL vs SQLite web mode
Keep TUI fallback available for any flows deferred from the web

high: Write-path bugs would damage trust faster than missing read-only features
Wallet rename/merge behavior is tax-sensitive and must remain exact
medium: Ledger UX can become cluttered quickly on phone-sized screens
Edit/delete flows require careful confirmation design to avoid accidental misuse
low: Core write/query behavior already exists in Python and is covered by tests
The TUI provides a proven fallback workflow during incremental rollout
